steps.text: Sift flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt into a large bowl. Whisk milk and egg together in a small bowl until well blended; stir into flour mixture until just combined. Stir in melted butter, then fold in blueberries.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle or nonstick frying pan over medium-high heat.
Pour or scoop batter onto the hot griddle, using about 1/4 cup per pancake. Cook until bubbles appear on the surface, then flip and cook until the bottom is golden brown. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Todd’s Famous Blueberry Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These fluffy blueberry pancakes are simple, delicious, and bursting with juicy blueberries. Drizzle with maple syrup for a family-pleasing breakfast!
raw_recipe.name: Todd’s Famous Blueberry Pancakes

review.reviewBody: These really are great, tender pancakes. I have made them several times and I feel it is necessary to mention that fresh blueberries are best, and that there is no need to wait the hour until making them! I have found that sprinkling the berries on the pancake after it is on the griddle works best and avoids smashing them. You can also use vegetable oil instead of the melted butter; it makes no difference, especially if you butter them afterwards anyway!

Can you say "YUM"? This is a top of the line blueberry pancake recipe. It always comes out perfect--fluffy, yet not cake-like. It's very moist with the blueberries; not a dry pancake at all. I even made it without the blueberries one time because we ran out, and it was delicious, too. But the blueberries put it in first gear! I've made it about a dozen times so far. Yes, the other reviews are correct in that you don't have to wait an hour to cook it--you don't even have to wait at all. They taste the same either way.

Turned out nice! I took another’s suggestion and added 2 T sugar instead of recipe amount. And added my rinsed and drained frozen blueberries to the dry ingredients before adding liquid. Liquid- my hubby like thinner pancakes so I also added an extra egg and a little extra milk. Also added 1 tsp vanilla.

Because I am lazy, I rushed the recipe and mixed all the ingredients together at indecency then immediately cooked the pancakes. And guess what? They turned out great! I used fresh blueberries instead of frozen and as mentioned previously, didn’t wait the hour and they turned out fluffy and great. Excellent recipe!

This is an above average pancakes-from-scratch recipe. I loved the idea to let the mixture sit for 45 minutes before cooking. It made for a firmer and better-cooked pancake. I added real vanilla extract, which made them better.

This is my regular, go-to pancake for weekend mornings. I've tried many recipes and these are the fluffiest. Fresh blueberries and pure maple syrup take them to the next level! Also, I use coconut oil instead of butter and it gives them an aromatic hint that we love! Agree with some of the other reviews that it's not necessary to wait the hour upfront. And I don't mix the blueberries into the batter, I just drop them in while the pancake is cooking on the griddle.

I have been hunting for a good pancake recipe and ive finally found it! I did make some changes based on others' recommendations: I increased the sugar to 1 tablespoon and added 1 teaspoon on vanilla extract to the milk and egg mixture. I used fresh blueberries but waited to add them once the pancakes were on the griddle. I think letting the batter sit for an hour is key. I'll be making these again!

Delicious, light, not-too-sweet pancakes. The hour resting time is crucial. Try to use fresh berries. No bleed, much better than frozen, but if frozen is all you have don't hesitate to make anyway. I added the fresh berries immediately after ladling the batter on, not at the initial mix. This recipe made eight roughly 4 - 5" pancakes, so at two pancakes per serving (I could've eaten more) this served four for us. Great recipe, thanks.

Been making these on and off for years. Recently used clarified butter instead of oil or reg. butter on the griddle. Just melted a few tbsps in the microwave and spooned off most of the solids and brushed on. No excessive browning at 375 deg. Nice slight butter flavor. Wait only 1/2 hr. Now these are my go-to pancakes.

I doubled the recipe to make nine pancakes, added the zest of a lemon with the milk and egg, and let sit ~20 minutes before starting to cook. Serve with roasted pecans to balance the sweetness. Family wouldn't stop raving about how good they were!

Okay, I didn't read the part where it said to set aside for 1 hour before cooking. I made it right away and it was GOOD. Didn't really tweak the recipe because it was actually my first time making pancakes. I used about 2/3 cup of blueberries (instead of 1/2 cup), and used about 1tsp of sugar (instead of 1.25tsp). In any case, this was SO delicious and simple. Will definitely make it again!
I added,a,Tsp of Mexican Vanilla, absolutely delicious.
The batter was to thick. It was a long process to try to cook them all the way.
great! adding the butter in before the blueberries was a nice touch, it really smoothed out the batter

I haven't eaten the pancakes yet but just wanted to say that there's no way this is going to make 12 pancakes. I just cut the recipe in half because I thought six pancakes would be plenty for me but it turned out only making three 4-in pancakes.
Easy to make and will be saving the recipe ❤️

Not sure if the ingredients are listef correctly? One Tablespoon of baking powder and 1- 1/2 tsp of sugar?? I followed the recipe exactly and pancakes were not good. Very heavy and not fluffy at all. Lacked flavor and did not brown nicely. Definitely don't waste your ingredients and time.
